The Tornados fue un grupo británico instrumental nacido en la década de los 60', cuyo estilo se define como Surf Rock. Su single más reconocido fue "Telstar" el que llegó a escalar hasta el puesto número uno en los rankings de los Estados Unidos y el Reino Unido. Con la salida de Heinz Burt

scenes.name: Joe Meek
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Productor independiente pionero en el mundo cerrado de la industria británica, trabajaba solo en un piso de Holloway Road con una compresión feroz y sonidos extraterrestres: «Johnny Remember Me» de John Leyton (1961), cantada por un hombre a un hombre, y «Telstar» de los Tornados (1962), número 1 a ambos lados del Atlántico. Sensible, casi clarividente, con un genio violento, vivió perseguido (real e imaginariamente): detenido en 1963 por «importunar» en un urinario, chantajeado, adicto a las anfetaminas, obsesionado con micrófonos ocultos, el ocultismo y los cementerios; los derechos de «Telstar» quedaron congelados por un pleito. Tras los Beatles su sonido parecía pasado. El 12 de agosto de 1966 salió el último disco de los Tornados con él, «Is That a Ship I Hear?», con olas y gaviotas para los piratas; nadie lo quiso. En la cara B, «Do You Come Here Often?», tras dos minutos de órgano, dos voces camp se pelean en un club gay de Londres: el primer disco de una gran discográfica británica con un retrato tan exacto de la vida homosexual. Su salud mental empeoró ese otoño, con deudas y amenazas de gánsteres.
scenes.family: Pop de estudio: Spector, Beach Boys, Meek

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

mentions.author: Jon Savage
mentions.text: Just when the pirates’ influence on the British charts was at its height, it seemed like a good angle. However, this was neither the Tornados’ nor Joe Meek’s time. Dylan’s Blonde on Blonde was released that week. The music papers were full of this landmark album, but the Tornados got short shrift: ‘Good of its kind and doubtless a hit three years ago, but not for today’s market’; ‘Somebody must be joking.’ The unkindest cuts…

mentions.author: Jon Savage
mentions.text: …the group, while in the ‘Blind Date’ feature – where artists were played new records without being told who they were by – Billy Fury guessed it was the Tornados. ‘It’s about time they changed the sound,’ he sniffed. ‘There’s none of the original members of the group in it now anyway so they shouldn’t be playing this sort of gear. It’s about five years out of date.’ There was a bit of needle here from 1962, when the Tornados had been Fury’s backing band, a relationship sundered by the bickering between Joe Meek and Fury’s manager Larry Parnes. But the singer was correct: it had been a long slow fall since ‘Telstar’, through seven flop singles. By 1966, the Tornados had shed all the original members, so Meek simply found another group, called the Saxons, and renamed them. Despite a rhythm stolen from Dave Dee, Dozy, Beaky, Mick and Tich’s smash hit ‘Hold Tight’, the Tornados’ rinky-dink instrumental had no chance. podcast.title: Connection to Muse's Matt Bellamy
podcast.body: The rhythm guitarist in The Tornados was George Bellamy. Sixteen years later, George had a son named Matt, who in 1994 formed a band that became known as Muse. "16 years later, George had a son named Matt. And in 1994, Matt formed a band that became known as Meek's."

podcast.title: First UK #1 in USA
podcast.body: The Tornados, with their Joe Meek-produced hit "Telstar," achieved the distinction of being the first British act to have a song reach number one in the United States. This historic feat occurred in 1962, notably predating the widespread success and phenomenon of the British Invasion. "La canción fue todo unito al convertirse en el primer número 1 en Estados Unidos, proveniente de Inglaterra, adelantándose también a la British Invasion."

srcs.episode: El productor que escuchó el nuevo mundo. Joe Meek.

xref.title: Murder-Suicide (February 3, 1967)
xref.body: On February 3, 1967, the eighth anniversary of Buddy Holly's death, Joe Meek used a shotgun, owned by the bassist of The Tornados, to kill his landlady before taking his own life. "On February 3, 1967, which, by the way, just happened to be the eighth anniversary of Buddy Holly's death, he grabbed a few of his friends. To shotgun, owned by the base player of a band called the Tornados, killed his landlady and then himself."
